era: Genesis / Master System / Game Gear / Nintendo 3DS / modern platforms
summary: Sega and Dotemu's urban beat-'em-up series, from the Genesis/Bare Knuckle trilogy through Lizardcube and Guard Crush's modern sequel.

entries.title: Streets of Rage
entries.definitive_edition: 3D Streets of Rage plus Master System supplement

emulation.emulator: Nintendo 3DS hardware / Genesis Plus GX / BlastEm
emulation.notes: Use 3DS for official feature set, or Genesis emulation for baseline preservation.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: 3DS 3D Classics feature set or accurate Genesis emulation

primary.why: The Genesis original is the baseline, but the Nintendo 3DS 3D Classics release adds stereoscopic 3D, Bare Knuckle Japanese-version mode, one-hit-kill mode, CRT mode, and restore points. The Master System version has a unique boss and different one-player design, so it is a supplement.
primary.how_to_play: Play 3D Streets of Rage on 3DS where owned; use Genesis/Sega Genesis Classics if 3DS eShop access is unavailable, then sample Master System for its unique boss route.

secondary.exclusive_content: Unique Round 6 boss and different one-player 8-bit design
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the Master System version for its unique boss and altered structure.
secondary.why: It is not the fidelity route, but it has source-documented unique content.

entries.remaster_caveats: Fan remakes are unofficial and not treated as best-version routes.

entries.title: Streets of Rage 2

emulation.emulator: Nintendo 3DS hardware / Genesis Plus GX / BlastEm
emulation.notes: Use 3DS for the official extra-mode route, or Genesis emulation for baseline play.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: 3DS 3D Classics feature set or accurate Genesis emulation

primary.why: The Genesis/Mega Drive version is the classic baseline, but M2's 3DS release adds stereoscopic 3D plus Rage Relay and Casual Mode, making it the most feature-complete official release. The 8-bit Master System and Game Gear versions are distinct enough to preserve as secondary curiosities.
primary.how_to_play: Play 3D Streets of Rage 2 on 3DS where owned; use Sega Genesis Classics or accurate Genesis emulation if 3DS access is unavailable.

secondary.exclusive_content: Different 8-bit adaptations from the Mega Drive original and from each other
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the 8-bit ports after the main game if you want their altered layouts/limitations.
secondary.why: They are not definitive, but they are substantially different.

entries.remaster_caveats: No full remake exists; fan remakes are unofficial.

emulation.notes: Use the Japanese version for the main playthrough; translation aids are optional but not official release content.

primary.platform: Sega Genesis / Mega Drive (Japanese Bare Knuckle III)
primary.why: The Japanese Bare Knuckle III release retains Ash as a normal playable character route, original colors/sound effects, and lower difficulty, while the Western Streets of Rage 3 altered graphics/sound, raised difficulty, and removed Ash from normal play. The Japanese version is therefore the completeness primary.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese Bare Knuckle III cartridge/ROM through original hardware, MiSTer, Genesis Plus GX, BlastEm, or a collection route that supports the Japanese version.

entries.title: Streets of Rage 4
entries.definitive_edition: Windows release with Mr. X Nightmare DLC

primary.version: PC release with Mr. X Nightmare DLC
primary.why: Streets of Rage 4 launched across Switch, PS4, Windows, Xbox One, and later Linux/macOS, Stadia, Android, and iOS. The Mr. X Nightmare expansion adds Survival Mode, training options, and additional playable characters, so the Windows version with DLC is the highest-fidelity and most complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version with Mr. X Nightmare installed; use console/mobile versions only if local play setup or portability matters more.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a new sequel, not a remake of the Genesis trilogy; fan remake projects are unofficial.
